text:
alex: quick heads-up — the node SDK sampleapp lost x-request-id in logs after we turned on OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation. repro below.

lee: do you mean the header-style request id (x-request-id) or our internal request_id field?

alex: header-style. our winston logger used to include reqId from middleware. after otel auto-instrument, logs show no reqId for downstream async handlers.

priya: which node sdk + opentelemetry package versions? this sounds like an async_hooks/context propagation issue.

alex: redwood-node v0.7.4, @opentelemetry/sdk-node v1.10.0, express + express-http-instrumentation. repro snippet:```js
// express middleware order
app.use(require('request-id')()); // sets req.id -> res.locals.reqId
app.use(redwood.middleware()); // attaches client and logging context
// enable otel auto-instrumentation later in setup
```

max: ordering matters a lot here. otel auto-instrumentation patches http/express and creates spans but doesn't automatically merge existing logging contexts. If our logger relies on async-local-storage and otel switches the async context, the logger won't see the original store.

priya: yup. we had a bug in the node sdk where we created a new AsyncLocalStorage per request when otel already created one. that clobbers the stored reqId. Fix is to reuse OTEL's context or share a single ALS instance.

alex: can we detect that and at least log a warning during init? onboarding folks keep hitting this and it breaks demos.

lee: also seeing complaints about redaction being too aggressive on sample data. an order-ref like ORD-2025-0001 becomes [REDACTED]. breaks demo flows.

max: our redaction regex is currently: `/([A-Z0-9\-]{8,})/` which is too broad. we should tighten it to only redact patterns that match known secret prefixes (sk_live_, sk_test_, jwt patterns) or use allowlists for dev.

priya: suggestion: add REDWOOD_REDACTION_MODE env var with options: strict|default|dev. dev = minimal redaction, strict = current paranoid regex. Also add a telemetry flag that reports redaction hits (no PII) so we can tune patterns.

alex: for a hotfix I'm going to: (1) change init order in sampleapp docs to enable otel before request-id middleware; (2) add detection + warning if request-id not found in logger context; (3) set REDWOOD_REDACTION_MODE=dev in onboarding templates.

lee: can you include a small script that asserts the header survives through async/await and promise-based handlers? those are where we saw drops.

alex: yes, quick mocha test covering express + async route + next tick and setTimeout. will push later today.

priya: long-term: SDK should expose a function to attach to existing OTEL context provider instead of creating its own. I'll open an RFC to standardize that for node and python parity.

max: ping me on the RFC. I have a branch where we wrap ALS to reuse existing contexts and fallback to our own if none exists. Works for worker threads too.

ci-bot: build queued for branch fix/node-otel-reqid (sha: a9b3c1) :gear:

alex: thanks y'all. once we land the fix can we update the quickstart guides and sampleapp docker-compose so new users don't hit this during workshops? it's been a good onboarding friction point. :pray:

lee: agreed. small docs change + one e2e in CI should catch regressions.

priya: i'll add e2e matrix: node versions 14/16/18 + otel enabled/disabled + REDWOOD_REDACTION_MODE=dev/strict. should cover most weirdness.

max: electrode: also logging level defaults in sampleapp are INFO; suggest setting to DEBUG in local quickstart so folks can see context warnings.

alex: perfect — will update the sampleapp README and the onboarding checklist.
